caption: Examples of good and poor fitness prediction performance. (a) On a thermostability dataset of mutants of a patient-derived antibody that cross-neutralizes SARS-CoV-1 and 2, the language model correctly assigns higher confidence (lower perplexity) to the high melting temperature antibody variants (r = −0.84, ρ = −0.88, τ = −0.73). (b) On an immunogenicity dataset of percent anti-drug antibody responses (% ADA) from administered antibody therapeutics, the language model incorrectly assigns both high and low confidences to therapeutics that produce a 0% ADA response (r = 0.48, ρ = 0.32, τ = 0.23).

caption: Summary of performance for each model-dataset pair. Pearson’s correlation coefficients (PCCs) for various protein model perplexities with a) aggregation, b) binding affinity, c) expression, d) immunogenicity, e) polyreactivity, and f) thermostability fitness prediction.
